transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I am here because things at work have gotten... well, I am a transportation inspector for the county, and it really all started after I got the county safety award. Which, by the way, they handed out at this big banquet hall out on Route 9, and the food was just terrible. Dry chicken, you know? My buddy Dave from zoning said the exact same thing, and he eats anything. We usually go to this diner after bowling on Thursdays and he orders the most burnt meatloaf. 

But anyway, ever since that award, certain people at my office have been twisting my inspection reports. Like, I check the undercarriages on the transit buses, and you have to be thorough. I saw this whole special on TV about a bus crash in the nineties that was completely avoidable if they just did basic rust checks. You can never be too careful with public transit. 

But now these guys are asking me all these pointed budget questions, acting like they are trying to make me look crooked or something. And my supervisor just brushes it off. He tells me it is just a normal review. He always says that while drinking this awful hazelnut coffee that stinks up the whole breakroom. I keep telling maintenance they need to fix the exhaust vent in there, but nobody ever listens to me about the HVAC system. 

But yeah, even with my supervisor saying it is a normal review, I can tell there is a coordinated effort to discredit me. It is pretty obvious what they are all doing.
Do you think these people at your office are specifically targeting you?

Oh, absolutely. It is a hundred percent targeted at me. Like I was saying, they are taking my specific inspection reports and twisting them around, asking me all these pointed budget questions to make me look crooked. Which is crazy because I don't even handle the budget! That is Brenda's department. 

Brenda sits over by the elevator, and she always wears these really loud, heavy silver bracelets. Every time she types on her keyboard, it’s just *clack, jingle, clack, jingle*. It drives me absolutely nuts. I told her once she should take them off while she works, but she just gave me this dirty look. People are so sensitive about everything now. Like my neighbor, Gary, he got all bent out of shape last week because I parked my truck a little too close to his property line. It’s a public street! I drive a 2018 Ford, great truck, never had transmission issues or anything like my old Chevy did. I had to replace the alternator on that Chevy three times. 

But anyway... what was I... right, the office. Even with my supervisor trying to tell me it’s just a normal review, I'm not an idiot. I can tell there is a coordinated effort to discredit me. They know I actually do my job right, so they have to come after me.
Do you think there's any possibility that you might be misinterpreting the actions of your coworkers?

Misinterpreting? No, no way. I mean, look, I know how things work. Ever since I got that county safety award, it's been clear as day. They take my inspection reports, the ones I spend hours on, and they twist them. They start asking these really specific, pointed budget questions just to make me look like I'm doing something crooked. 

Speaking of crooked, you should see the way they paved the new parking lot at the depot. It's totally slanted toward the storm drain, but they missed the drain by like two feet! So every time it rains, there's this massive puddle right where I park. I told the facilities guy—Frank, I think his name is, always wears those suspenders with the little tools printed on them—I told him they need to regrade it, but he just ignored me. Just like he ignores the fact that the vending machine in the breakroom has been eating quarters for three weeks. I lost a whole dollar trying to get a bag of pretzels on Tuesday. I love those sourdough pretzels, the really crunchy ones. My dentist told me I need to be careful with hard foods because I have a crown on my back molar. Got it done last year, cost me a fortune out of pocket because the county dental plan is a joke. 

But no, I'm not misinterpreting anything at the office. My supervisor tries to play it down, tells me it's just a "normal review" process. But I'm not blind. I can tell there is a totally coordinated effort to discredit me. They're all in on it.
Do you think it's possible that your coworkers are just doing their jobs and not actually out to get you?

Just doing their jobs? No, that doesn't make any sense. If they were just doing their jobs, why would they be taking my specific inspection reports and twisting them all around? It started right after I got that county safety award. They started asking me all these pointed budget questions, completely out of nowhere, acting like I'm doing something crooked. 

Which is exactly what I said to my brother, Mike, when we were out fishing last weekend. We were up at Miller's Pond. He caught this massive largemouth bass, had to be at least four pounds. I didn't catch anything, just a bunch of weeds. I was using these new spinnerbaits I bought online, but I think the color was wrong for the water clarity. The water was super murky because of all the rain we had on Friday. It rained so hard my gutters overflowed. I need to get up on the ladder and clean them out, but my ladder is super wobbly. It's one of those aluminum extension ones, and one of the rubber feet fell off. I tried taping a piece of wood to the bottom, but it's just not safe. You really can't mess around with ladder safety. My uncle fell off a roof in the eighties and broke his collarbone, and he still complains about it when it gets cold out. 

But anyway, no, they aren't just doing their jobs. My supervisor keeps trying to tell me it's a normal review, but I know better. It's obvious there's a coordinated effort to discredit me. They're trying to make me look bad, plain and simple.
Do you think there's anyone outside of your office who might be involved in this effort to discredit you?

Outside the office? I... I don't think so. I haven't really noticed anyone else getting involved. It's mostly just the people at work who are twisting my reports and asking those budget questions. I mean, I guess I wouldn't put it past them to talk to people, but so far, no, just the office people. 

Although, you know, it makes you wonder who you can trust these days. Like, I went to the hardware store on Saturday to get a new rubber foot for that ladder I was telling you about. The guy working there, young kid, maybe eighteen, he tried to sell me a whole new ladder! I told him, "Look, buddy, the aluminum is perfectly fine, I just need the foot." But he kept pushing this fiberglass one, saying it was safer around power lines. I don't even work around power lines! I live in a neighborhood where all the utilities are buried underground. They did that back in the nineties. It looks so much cleaner, you know? But anyway, I ended up just buying a roll of heavy-duty duct tape and some thick rubber padding to fix it myself. Cost me like eight bucks instead of a hundred and fifty. You really have to watch your wallet with these retail places, they always try to upsell you. 

But no, to answer your question, it's just the people at the office trying to discredit me. I haven't seen anyone else doing it.
Why do you think your coworkers want to discredit you?

Why do they want to? Well, it's jealousy, pure and simple. It all started right after I got that county safety award. Before that, I was just another inspector, but then I get recognized, and suddenly they're looking at me sideways. They take my inspection reports and they twist the facts, making up these pointed budget questions out of thin air just to make it look like I'm doing something crooked. 

Speaking of crooked, my cousin Jimmy tried to fix the alignment on his truck last weekend by himself in his driveway. I told him, "Jimmy, you can't just eyeball a front-end alignment," but he wouldn't listen. He drove it down to the diner—the one on Route 9, they make those huge omelets, you know, with the home fries cooked right inside the egg? I always get the Western omelet, but I ask them to hold the green peppers because they give me terrible heartburn. I have to take those little pink pills if I eat peppers, and they taste like chalk. Anyway, Jimmy drove his truck there and the steering wheel was shaking so bad he spilled his coffee all over the center console. Serves him right for not taking it to a real mechanic. I always go to this guy Sal over in Westville, he's honest. 

But yeah, the people at the office, they aren't honest like Sal. My supervisor tries to smooth it over, tells me it's just a "normal review" process and that I shouldn't take it personally. But I'm not stupid. I can tell there's a coordinated effort to discredit me because they can't stand that I got that award.
Do you think your coworkers would be treating you this way if you hadn't received the county safety award?

No way. If I hadn't gotten that award, I'd still just be flying under the radar. This whole thing has been going on for about a year, ever since I got recognized for the county safety initiative. 

Speaking of safety stuff, that reminds me, I had to replace all the smoke detectors in my house last week. The old ones started doing that low-battery chirp at like three in the morning. Have you ever tried to figure out which detector is chirping in the dark? It echoes down the hallway, so you can't even tell where it's coming from. I was standing on a kitchen chair in my boxers for twenty minutes just waiting for it to beep again so I could track it down. Turns out it was the one in the spare room where I keep my old baseball card collection. I've got a Ken Griffey Jr. rookie card in there that's gotta be worth something by now. My dad bought it for me at a card show back before he moved down to Florida. He's always trying to get me to come visit him in Tampa, but the humidity down there is just brutal. I went down there once in August and I swear I sweat through two shirts before lunch. Plus, the palmetto bugs down there are basically the size of small birds. It's disgusting. 

But anyway, yeah, it's been about a year of them treating me like this at work, all because I got recognized for that initiative. If I hadn't won it, they wouldn't care about me at all.
Do you think your coworkers' behavior towards you would change if you were to leave your current job and work somewhere else?

If I left? Yeah, I think if I went somewhere else, it would stop. I mean, they're just jealous of me here. If I went to a new department or a different county, nobody there would care about the safety award, so they wouldn't have any reason to twist my reports. 

Actually, I was thinking about transferring over to the parks department a while back. They get to drive those little utility carts around all day. My buddy Steve has a golf cart he souped up. He put a lift kit on it and these big knobby tires. We took it out on the trails behind his house last weekend, and let me tell you, that thing can climb! We got stuck in the mud though, right up to the axles. We had to use a winch to pull it out, and Steve ended up ruining a brand new pair of boots. They were those expensive leather ones, you know, the kind you have to oil every month or they crack? I told him he should have just worn rubber boots, but he's always trying to look sharp. He even wears cologne when we go fishing. It's ridiculous. The fish don't care what you smell like! 

But yeah, if I left this job, I'm pretty sure the new people wouldn't be out to get me. It's just this specific group at my office.
Do you think your coworkers would be talking about you or plotting against you even when you're not at work?

Oh, absolutely. They don't just stop when the clock hits five. I know they're texting each other, coordinating the whole thing on the weekends or at night. That's probably when they come up with all those pointed budget questions to throw at me on Monday morning. They spend their time off trying to figure out how to twist my inspection reports to make me look crooked. My supervisor keeps telling me it's just a normal review process, but you don't do normal reviews by plotting behind someone's back after hours. It's a coordinated effort to discredit me, plain and simple. 

Speaking of texting, I actually had to go to the mall this weekend to get my phone screen fixed. I dropped it right on the concrete floor at Home Depot. I was in the plumbing aisle looking for a new P-trap for my bathroom sink—the old one was leaking all over the inside of the vanity, ruined a perfectly good stack of towels. They were those thick, Egyptian cotton ones too, my aunt got them for me for Christmas a couple years ago. She always buys me towels or socks, like I don't know how to shop for myself, you know? She means well, but still. 

Anyway, the guy at the phone repair kiosk charged me eighty bucks just for a little piece of glass. What a racket. He had this little machine that supposedly gets the air bubbles out, but I can still see a tiny one right in the top corner of my screen. It drives me crazy every time I open my email. 

But yeah, anyway... they're definitely talking about me when I'm not at the office. They wouldn't put in all this effort just during business hours.
Would you change your mind about people being out to get you if someone you trust told you that your coworkers are actually just trying to do their jobs?

No, I wouldn't. I mean, my supervisor already tried telling me that. He says it's just a normal review process, but I can tell there's a coordinated effort to discredit me. Even if someone I trust said it, it wouldn't change what I see happening. Ever since I got that county safety award, certain people have been twisting my inspection reports and asking all those pointed budget questions just to make me look crooked. You can't just ignore that kind of stuff. 

Speaking of trust, I used to trust this mechanic down the street, Gary. I took my truck to him for years. But last month, I brought it in for an oil change, and he tried to tell me I needed a whole new transmission. Can you believe that? A whole new transmission on a truck with only sixty thousand miles on it! I told him he was out of his mind. I ended up taking it to a guy my buddy Steve recommended, and all it needed was a little transmission fluid. Saved me like two grand. 

I took that money I saved and bought a new grill for the backyard. It's one of those big gas ones with the side burner. I've been trying to perfect my rib recipe. I use a dry rub with brown sugar and paprika, and then I slow-cook them for like four hours. They fall right off the bone. I made a batch last weekend and invited Steve over, but he ended up getting a stomach bug and couldn't make it. So I had to eat ribs for three days straight. Not that I'm complaining, but you get tired of pork after a while. 

But yeah, anyway, even if someone I trusted told me my coworkers were just doing their jobs, I wouldn't buy it. I know what they're doing. They're trying to ruin me because of that award.
Did your coworkers behave differently towards you before you received the county safety award?

Yeah, they were totally normal before. This has been going on for about a year, ever since I got recognized for the county safety initiative. Before that, we'd joke around in the breakroom and stuff. But after I got that award... I mean, they gave me this plaque at the annual county dinner, and you could just feel the room get cold when my name was called. 

That dinner was out at the convention center, and man, the food they served was just terrible. They gave everyone this baked chicken that was so dry you practically needed a gallon of water to choke it down. I don't get why they can't just cater something good, like barbecue. 

Actually, speaking of barbecue, I just bought one of those new pellet smokers last month. The kind where you load the wood pellets in the side hopper and it feeds them in automatically? It even connects to an app on my phone, so I can check the temperature of the meat while I'm sitting inside on the couch watching TV. I made a brisket on it for the playoffs, smoked it for like fourteen hours. You gotta wrap it in pink butcher paper halfway through, not tin foil, otherwise the crust gets all mushy. The paper lets it breathe. I had to drive to three different stores just to find the right kind of unwaxed paper, though. The kid working at the hardware store tried to sell me brown packing paper, like I was gonna wrap my expensive brisket in a cardboard box. People just don't know what they're talking about half the time. 

But anyway, yeah... before that safety initiative a year ago, they didn't treat me like this at all.
Did your coworkers start acting differently towards you immediately after you received the county safety award, or was it sometime after that?

It was pretty much right away. Like I said, this whole thing has been going on for about a year, ever since I got recognized for that county safety initiative. The second I walked back into the office with that plaque, it was like a switch flipped. 

I actually still have the plaque sitting on my desk, right next to this little cactus my mom gave me. She brought it over when I moved into my new apartment. She said it was good for the air quality or something, but honestly, I think she just wanted to give me something I couldn't kill. I'm terrible with plants. I tried growing tomatoes on my balcony last summer, and the squirrels got to every single one of them before they even turned red. Those little guys are relentless. I tried putting cayenne pepper on the soil, because I read online that it keeps them away, but I swear it just seasoned the tomatoes for them. 

My buddy Steve told me I should get a pellet gun to scare them off, but I live in an apartment complex, you know? I can't just be shooting out my sliding glass door. The property manager is already on my case because I left my mountain bike chained to the railing for a week. I meant to bring it inside, but the chain popped off the gears when I was riding some trails out at Miller's Woods, and my hands were so covered in grease I didn't want to touch the door handle. 

But yeah, anyway, the change in them was immediate. About a year ago, right after I got the award.
Have you ever experienced any actual threats or harmful actions from your coworkers?

No, not like physical threats or anything like that. They're too smart for that. It's all behind my back, messing with the inspection reports, asking those budget questions to make me look bad. But nobody's actually come up and threatened me to my face. 

I don't think they'd have the guts anyway. Most of those guys wouldn't know what to do in a real confrontation. Like this one time I was at the grocery store, just trying to get some charcoal for the grill, right? And this guy in a pickup truck just whips into the parking spot I was waiting for with my blinker on. I laid on the horn, and he gets out and starts yelling at me, waving his hands around. I just rolled down my window and stared at him, didn't say a word. He got so flustered he just muttered something and walked into the store. People talk a big game until you actually stand your ground. 

I ended up having to park way out in the back of the lot, which was a pain because I was buying two of those huge twenty-pound bags of Kingsford. The blue bags, not the match-light stuff. That match-light charcoal makes your food taste like lighter fluid, it's disgusting. I don't know why they even sell it. You just need a chimney starter and some newspaper, and you're good to go. I usually save the weekly circulars they leave on my door just for that. The property manager gets mad if you leave them sitting out there too long, but they're perfect for starting the grill. 

But no, to answer your question, no actual threats from the guys at work. Just the coordinated stuff to ruin my reputation.
Did your coworkers start treating you differently right after you received the county safety award, or was there a delay before you noticed the change?

Yeah, like I was saying, it was pretty much right away. No delay at all. This whole thing has been going on for about a year, ever since I got recognized for the county safety initiative. The change was instant. 

It reminds me of when my buddy Steve got his new truck. One day he's driving this beat-up old sedan, and the next day he rolls up in this massive lifted F-150. Instant change. He had to get special step bars just to climb into the thing. We took it out to Miller's Woods a couple weeks ago to test the four-wheel drive, and man, that thing can handle some serious mud. We ended up getting stuck, though, because Steve thought he could cross this creek bed that was way deeper than it looked. The water came right up to the doors. We had to call a tow truck to winch us out, and the driver charged us like two hundred bucks just for coming out there on a Sunday. 

Steve was so mad, he tried to argue with the guy, but what are you gonna do? You're stuck in the mud. Kind of like how I feel at work sometimes, you know? Just stuck. But yeah, to answer your question, it's been about a year since they started acting like this, right after I got the award.
Have you ever felt like people were out to get you in situations outside of your job?

No, not really. It's just the guys at work. Outside of that, things are pretty normal. I mean, nobody's following me around the grocery store or anything. 

Speaking of the grocery store, I was actually just there yesterday trying to find those specific jalapeño kettle chips I like. They're the only ones that actually have a good kick to them. Most brands say "spicy" but they just taste like vinegar and paprika. But this one brand, I think it's a local company, they actually use real jalapeño powder. Anyway, they were completely out. The shelf was totally bare. I asked the kid stocking the soda aisle if they had any in the back, and he just gave me this blank stare like I was asking him to solve a math problem. Kids these days, man, they just don't have any customer service skills. 

My first job was at a hardware store, and if someone asked for a specific size of carriage bolt, you didn't just stare at them, you went and found it. Or you at least pretended to look in the back. I learned so much about plumbing and electrical stuff working there. It really helped when I moved into my apartment because the sink was leaking underneath, right at the P-trap. The maintenance guy said it would take a week to get to it, so I just went to the hardware store, bought a new PVC trap for like four bucks, and fixed it myself in ten minutes. The maintenance guy was actually pretty impressed when he finally showed up. 

But yeah, no, it's just the guys at the office who are trying to mess with me. I don't feel like anyone else is out to get me.
Do you feel like people are out to get you in other parts of your life, outside of work?

I mean, I think I just said that, right? No, it's really just the guys at the office. Outside of work, everything's totally fine. I don't have any problems with anyone else. 

Like my neighbors, they're great. The guy next door, Mr. Henderson, he actually just retired last month. He used to work for the post office for like thirty-five years. He was telling me about how much the routes have changed and how they track everything with GPS now. It's crazy how much technology has taken over. He bought this massive RV to celebrate his retirement. A Winnebago, I think. It takes up like four parking spaces in the back lot, but the property manager let it slide because he's been living here so long. 

He's planning to drive it all the way up to Alaska next summer. I told him he's crazy for driving something that big on those mountain roads, especially with the gas prices right now. I drive a Honda Civic and it still costs me forty bucks to fill the tank. I used to have an old Jeep Wrangler, you know, the ones with the square headlights? I loved that thing, but the gas mileage was terrible. I think I got maybe fourteen miles to the gallon on a good day. Plus, the soft top always leaked when it rained, right on the driver's seat. You'd get in to go to work and just sit in a puddle. 

But yeah, no, I don't think anyone else is out to get me. It's just the guys at work who are pulling this stuff. Everyone else is fine.
Do you feel like you're being targeted or treated unfairly in any other areas of your life besides work?

Didn't you just ask me that? Or something like it? No, like I keep saying, it's just the guys at the transit authority. Nobody else is doing this. I don't know why you keep asking about other people, my life outside the depot is completely normal. 

Actually, I was just at the laundromat this morning because my building's dryer is still broken. The landlord keeps saying he ordered the heating element, but it's been three weeks. Anyway, the lady who runs the laundromat, Maria, she's always super nice to me. She even saves the big front-loading washer for me if she knows I'm coming in on a Saturday. Those big machines are the best, you can fit like three loads in there at once. I hate doing laundry, so getting it all done in one shot is great. 

While I was waiting for my clothes, I walked over to that little diner on 4th Street to grab a coffee. They make this incredible blueberry coffee cake. The owner said it's his grandmother's recipe from back in Maine. I've never been to Maine, but I've always wanted to go see the lighthouses. My aunt went a few years ago and brought me back this little snow globe with a lighthouse in it. I used to collect snow globes when I was a kid. I had like fifty of them on these floating shelves in my bedroom. Then one day, the brackets gave out and the whole thing came crashing down. Glass and water everywhere. My mom was so mad because it ruined the hardwood floor. 

But anyway, yeah, I'm not being targeted anywhere else. Just at work. Just the guys who can't handle that I got the safety award.
Have you ever felt like someone was out to get you when you were not at work?

Are you... are you messing with me right now? I feel like I'm taking crazy pills. This is the fourth time you've asked me the exact same thing. No. No, nobody outside of work is out to get me. It's just the guys at the depot. I don't know how else to say it. 

I mean, if someone was following me around outside of work, my dog would definitely notice. I have a German Shepherd mix, Buster. He's incredibly protective. If anyone even walks down the hallway past my apartment, he's at the door, growling. He's got this really deep bark, sounds like a much bigger dog than he actually is. I adopted him from the shelter about two years ago. They said he was a stray, found him wandering around the industrial park near the old textile mill. 

The mill's been closed down since the nineties, I think. They keep talking about turning it into luxury lofts, but the zoning board keeps blocking it because of some environmental study about the soil. Something about chemicals they used to dye the fabrics. It's a shame, really, because the brickwork on that building is beautiful. You don't see craftsmanship like that anymore. Everything now is just cheap drywall and vinyl siding. When I was looking for an apartment, I specifically wanted an older building because the walls are thicker. You can't hear your neighbors breathing like you can in those new constructions. 

But look, doc, honestly, I'm getting a little frustrated here. I came to talk about what's happening to me at the transit authority, and you keep asking me about everywhere else. It's just work. Just work.
Have you ever felt like someone was out to get you when you were not thinking about work?

Okay, seriously? Is there a hidden camera in here or something? Because you literally just keep asking me the exact same question, just using slightly different words. No! Never. When I'm not thinking about work, I'm just living my life. Nobody is bothering me. 

Like yesterday, I wasn't thinking about work at all. I was just at the hardware store trying to find a specific type of Allen wrench. I bought this TV stand online, one of those cheap particle board ones, and they shorted me the tool to put it together. Typical, right? You try to save a few bucks and you end up spending two hours at Home Depot anyway. The guy working in the tool aisle was actually really helpful, though. Older guy, wore one of those orange aprons covered in little pins. He showed me this whole master set of hex keys that was on clearance. 

Honestly, you can never have too many tools. My grandpa used to have an entire pegboard in his garage where every single tool had its own outline drawn in black marker. If you didn't put the hammer back exactly inside the hammer outline, he'd lose his mind. He was a carpenter, built half the houses in his neighborhood back in the seventies. They don't build them like that anymore, all real wood, no cheap composites. He actually built this beautiful cedar chest for my mom when she got married. It still smells like cedar when you open it, even after all these years. 

But anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right. No. When I'm not at the depot, or thinking about the guys at the depot, everything is completely fine. I don't know why we keep going in circles with this.
Have you ever felt like someone was out to get you when you're alone at home?

Are you kidding me right now? Are you actually kidding me? Home? Work? Not work? Not thinking about work? It's the same question! You're asking me the exact same thing again! No! No one is out to get me at home. When I'm alone at home, I'm just... alone. 

I was just sitting on my couch last night, actually, watching this documentary about deep sea diving. It's crazy what people will do for fun, you know? Going down hundreds of feet in the pitch black. The pressure down there is insane. They were talking about how if a submarine gets even a tiny crack at that depth, the whole thing just implodes in like a fraction of a second. Boom. Gone. It made me think about this time I went to an aquarium when I was a kid, and they had this huge glass tunnel you walk through where the sharks swim right over your head. I was terrified the glass was going to break. The tour guide kept saying it was acrylic, not glass, and it was like six inches thick, but still. 

I don't know much about acrylics, honestly, but I do know a lot about safety glass. We have to inspect the windshields on the buses all the time. If there's a spiderweb crack larger than a quarter, the bus gets pulled from the route. Safety first, right? That's what I always say. That's why I got the award. 

But no, doc. For the last time. Nobody is after me at home. It's just the guys at the depot who are trying to ruin me. Can we please talk about them now?

Anyway, the lady who runs the laundromat, Maria, she's always super nice to me. She even saves the big front-loading washer for me if she knows I'm coming in on a Saturday. Those big machines are the best, you can fit like three loads in there at once. I hate doing laundry, so getting it all done in one shot is great. 

While I was waiting for my clothes, I walked over to that little diner on 4th Street to grab a coffee. They make this incredible blueberry coffee cake. The owner said it's his grandmother's recipe from back in Maine. I've never been to Maine, but I've always wanted to go see the lighthouses. My aunt went a few years ago and brought me back this little snow globe with a lighthouse in it. I used to collect snow globes when I was a kid. I had like fifty of them on these floating shelves in my bedroom. Then one day, the brackets gave out and the whole thing came crashing down. Glass and water everywhere. My mom was so mad because it ruined the hardwood floor. 

But anyway, yeah, I'm not being targeted anywhere else. Just at work. Just the guys who can't handle that I got the safety award.

patient.answer:
Are you... are you messing with me right now? I feel like I'm taking crazy pills. This is the fourth time you've asked me the exact same thing. No. No, nobody outside of work is out to get me. It's just the guys at the depot. I don't know how else to say it. 

I mean, if someone was following me around outside of work, my dog would definitely notice. I have a German Shepherd mix, Buster. He's incredibly protective. If anyone even walks down the hallway past my apartment, he's at the door, growling. He's got this really deep bark, sounds like a much bigger dog than he actually is. I adopted him from the shelter about two years ago. They said he was a stray, found him wandering around the industrial park near the old textile mill. 

The mill's been closed down since the nineties, I think. They keep talking about turning it into luxury lofts, but the zoning board keeps blocking it because of some environmental study about the soil. Something about chemicals they used to dye the fabrics. It's a shame, really, because the brickwork on that building is beautiful. You don't see craftsmanship like that anymore. Everything now is just cheap drywall and vinyl siding. When I was looking for an apartment, I specifically wanted an older building because the walls are thicker. You can't hear your neighbors breathing like you can in those new constructions. 

But look, doc, honestly, I'm getting a little frustrated here. I came to talk about what's happening to me at the transit authority, and you keep asking me about everywhere else. It's just work. Just work.

patient.answer:
Okay, seriously? Is there a hidden camera in here or something? Because you literally just keep asking me the exact same question, just using slightly different words. No! Never. When I'm not thinking about work, I'm just living my life. Nobody is bothering me. 

Like yesterday, I wasn't thinking about work at all. I was just at the hardware store trying to find a specific type of Allen wrench. I bought this TV stand online, one of those cheap particle board ones, and they shorted me the tool to put it together. Typical, right? You try to save a few bucks and you end up spending two hours at Home Depot anyway. The guy working in the tool aisle was actually really helpful, though. Older guy, wore one of those orange aprons covered in little pins. He showed me this whole master set of hex keys that was on clearance. 

Honestly, you can never have too many tools. My grandpa used to have an entire pegboard in his garage where every single tool had its own outline drawn in black marker. If you didn't put the hammer back exactly inside the hammer outline, he'd lose his mind. He was a carpenter, built half the houses in his neighborhood back in the seventies. They don't build them like that anymore, all real wood, no cheap composites. He actually built this beautiful cedar chest for my mom when she got married. It still smells like cedar when you open it, even after all these years. 

But anyway... what was I saying? Oh, right. No. When I'm not at the depot, or thinking about the guys at the depot, everything is completely fine. I don't know why we keep going in circles with this.

patient.answer:
Are you kidding me right now? Are you actually kidding me? Home? Work? Not work? Not thinking about work? It's the same question! You're asking me the exact same thing again! No! No one is out to get me at home. When I'm alone at home, I'm just... alone. 

I was just sitting on my couch last night, actually, watching this documentary about deep sea diving. It's crazy what people will do for fun, you know? Going down hundreds of feet in the pitch black. The pressure down there is insane. They were talking about how if a submarine gets even a tiny crack at that depth, the whole thing just implodes in like a fraction of a second. Boom. Gone. It made me think about this time I went to an aquarium when I was a kid, and they had this huge glass tunnel you walk through where the sharks swim right over your head. I was terrified the glass was going to break. The tour guide kept saying it was acrylic, not glass, and it was like six inches thick, but still. 

I don't know much about acrylics, honestly, but I do know a lot about safety glass. We have to inspect the windshields on the buses all the time. If there's a spiderweb crack larger than a quarter, the bus gets pulled from the route. Safety first, right? That's what I always say. That's why I got the award. 

But no, doc. For the last time. Nobody is after me at home. It's just the guys at the depot who are trying to ruin me. Can we please talk about them now?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's persistent belief that his coworkers are conspiring against him, despite lack of evidence and reassurance from his supervisor, suggests a delusional disorder. The focus of the delusion is persecutory, which is consistent with F22. While F23 (brief psychotic disorder) could be considered, the duration of the symptoms (about a year) and the lack of other psychotic symptoms make F22 a more appropriate diagnosis.
